resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Occupancy (CCO) for Sale of Residential Property
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Butler Zoning Department / Enforcement Officer
resale_co.lead_time: Minimum of 7 full business days notice required for inspections. The Enforcement Officer may waive the inspection and fee if the same premises was inspected within 60 days.
requirements: Inspection for compliance with the Borough Property Maintenance Code (Chapter 180), Land Use Ordinance, NJ Housing Code and NJ smoke detector regulations
House number clearly visible, at least 2 1/4 inches high and contrasting with the background

Pools and hot tubs: 48 inch fence or wall, self-closing self-latching gates opening out with release at least 54 inches high; zoning and construction permits on file (no CCO until permits are obtained and inspected)
Smoke and carbon monoxide alarms in proper working order (smoke/CO certification done with the CCO)
Secondary power source caution label near the main panel and meter if the home has a generator, solar panels or battery storage

fees.label: Residential sale CCO, per dwelling unit
fees.quote: (Fee is $200 per residential unit) FEE MUST ACCOMPANY APPLICATION.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Submit the CCO Application for Sale of Residential Property with the $200 per unit fee (cash or check payable to Borough of Butler, 1 Ace Rd; no credit cards at the counter), or apply and pay online through the Borough's E-Permits webforms. List the emails of the parties and attorneys; the approved CCO is e-mailed. Give a contact who will let the Fire Inspector in; allow at least 7 full business days for the inspection.

evidence.quote: CCO APPLICATION for SALE of RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY
(Fee is $200 per residential unit) FEE MUST ACCOMPANY APPLICATION.
Minimum of 7 Full Business Days Notice Required for Inspections!
Under Borough of Butler Ordinance, Chapter 143-177, a Continued Certificate of Occupancy is required.
No person shall sell, occupy, or use any portion of a commercial, industrial or residential building after such building or portion thereof has been vacated or sold,
The Enforcement Officer may waive the inspection and fee if any inspection of the same premises has been made within 60 days.
You can now apply for a Zoning Permit or a Residential Continued Certificate of Occupancy (CCO), Sale of Home & Rental CCO Permits online.

resale_co.notes: Butler Code Section 143-177C (amended July 16, 2024) bars selling or occupying a sold residential building until a certificate of continuing occupancy is issued. The current application (Rev. 7/2026) charges $200 per residential unit and covers the smoke/CO inspection by the Fire Inspector. The online Zoning page and Fire Prevention page link the application. No validity period is published.

requirements: Hardwired interconnected smoke alarms must be kept working and may not be converted to battery alarms
All smoke alarms less than 10 years old and UL listed; new battery alarms must be sealed 10-year units

At least one smoke alarm on every level including the basement and habitable attic, plus attics/crawl spaces containing fuel-burning equipment; alarms in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedroom doors
Carbon monoxide alarms on all levels with bedrooms, within 10 feet of all bedroom doors (hardwired, plug-in or battery)
Secondary power source caution label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter, if applicable
Fire extinguishers are no longer required (Borough form)

authorities.name: Butler Fire Prevention Bureau (inspection done with the Borough residential sale CCO)
authorities.lead_time: Minimum of 7 full business days notice for inspections.

fees.label: Smoke/CO reinspection after a failed inspection
fees.quote: there will be a $25 Re-Inspection Fee for each Inspection Failure regarding the Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Detectors.

fees.label: Smoke detector certification, resale (Borough fee schedule, Ord. 2000-26; the current CCO form shows only the $200 CCO fee)

authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke and CO inspection is requested on the Borough's CCO Application for Sale of Residential Property; the Fire Inspector contacts the person named on the form to set up the appointment. A $25 reinspection fee must be paid before a reinspection.

evidence.quote: there will be a $25 Re-Inspection Fee for each Inspection Failure regarding the Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Detectors.
FIRE EXTINGUISHERS ARE NO LONGER REQUIRED.

fire_cert.notes: Butler's smoke/CO check is part of the residential sale CCO: the application (Rev. 7/2026) names a Fire Inspector who schedules the inspection, says fire extinguishers are no longer required, and charges $25 for each failed smoke/CO inspection. Section 119-1 of the code book still lists a separate $50.00 'Smoke detector certification, resale' fee from 2000, and Sections 136-29J and 136-30C (Housing Standards) still require smoke/CO and fire extinguisher certificates from the Code Enforcer before a change in ownership; whether the $50 is charged on top of the $200 CCO fee is not stated. Fire Official Mark Lime also serves Pequannock Township.

other_items.label: Pool and hot tub permits
other_items.detail: If a pool or hot tub has no permits, the CCO will not be issued until permits are obtained and inspections pass.

open_questions: Is Butler's $50.00 resale smoke detector certification fee (code Section 119-1) still charged in addition to the $200 per unit CCO fee?
How long is the Butler residential sale CCO valid?
Are there short-notice (rush) fees for the smoke/CO inspection?
